title: Row-by-row PL/SQL is slow-by-slow: make a batch 52× faster in 6 steps (3h 10m → 3m 40s)
desc:
A nightly PL/SQL batch: 2,000,000 payments, 3 hours 10 minutes. The batch window: 1 hour 😱
Same logic, same result: 3 minutes 40 seconds at the end. Step by step.

🔍 Measure first: DBMS_APPLICATION_INFO module tags + V$SQL
   → no slow statement, just 8 million fast ones
⏳ Stop committing every row: log file sync = 52 minutes of waiting
🔁 BULK COLLECT … LIMIT 1000 + FORALL: 2,000 context switches instead of 2,000,000
🔗 Replace per-row lookups with a JOIN (HASH JOIN, rates read once)
🧩 One SQL statement: MERGE + INSERT … SELECT
   → DML error logging: LOG ERRORS INTO err$_ REJECT LIMIT UNLIMITED
⚡ Still too big? Parallel DML or DBMS_PARALLEL_EXECUTE chunks
✅ Verify: same counts and totals on a copy

3h 10m → 2h 18m → 38m → 14m → 6m → 3m 40s 💡
